name: Susan Mann
headline: Founder and president, Bright Minds Processing
on_the_show: Susan Mann told Dave and Mike how teachers called her two children gifted while every test put them near the bottom, until an audiologist identified auditory and visual processing disorders. A retired San Francisco police officer, not a clinician, she now runs Bright Minds Processing so other families get answers sooner. She described the therapy as 16 weeks, one session a week with exercises five evenings a week at home, starting with a $30 screening, and the basketball program she is building in Palm Beach Gardens with former NBA player Dwayne McClain.
on_the_show_quote: They can’t be gifted if they can’t do their schoolwork.

background.text: She is the founder and president of Bright Minds Processing, where she oversees the strategic direction and operations of the nonprofit.
Bright Minds Processing Inc. is a Florida 501(c)(3) nonprofit that works to raise awareness of auditory and visual processing disorders and to bring solutions into schools.
She started the organization after both of her children were diagnosed with auditory and visual processing disorders, a journey she tells in her own words on its site.
The organization runs the McClain Basketball Academy, led by former professional player Dwayne “D-Train” McClain, where students must keep their grades up to take part.
In April 2026 she appeared on CBS12’s ARC Florida with Dwayne McClain ahead of the group’s first fundraising event at the SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens.

Her site gives no city; Palm Beach Gardens comes from the CBS12 dateline and her own on-air description of the program she is setting up there.
